```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Kong 2025 gave a single oral microdose cocktail of five probe substrates to
Chinese healthy volunteers (HV) and haemodialysis-dependent end-stage renal
disease (ESRD) patients, and fitted one population PK model per drug to the
pooled pre-dialysis concentrations. The five models were fitted
independently, so they are packaged as five model files that share this
article.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kong_2025_pitavastatin"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.3546> (open access; PMC11993298)

| Model | Probe for | Covariates on the final model |
|-------|-----------|-------------------------------|
| `Kong_2025_pitavastatin` | OATP1B | ESRD and gut *Veillonella* abundance on CL/F |
| `Kong_2025_dabigatran` | intestinal P-gp (dose given as dabigatran etexilate) | ESRD on CL/F |
| `Kong_2025_rosuvastatin` | OATP1B / BCRP | gut *Clostridium* XIVb abundance on CL/F; serum albumin on Vc/F |
| `Kong_2025_midazolam` | CYP3A | ESRD on CL/F |
| `Kong_2025_atorvastatin` | CYP3A4 / OATP1B / P-gp / BCRP | none |

All five are two-compartment models with first-order absorption and
first-order elimination, parameterised as apparent oral values (CL/F, Vc/F,
Vp/F, Q/F). Doses are in ug and concentrations in pg/mL, the paper's units.

# Population

Fourteen HV (5 male, 9 female; mean age 35.6 years, BMI 22.4 kg/m^2, eGFR
106.6 mL/min/1.73 m^2) and ten ESRD patients on haemodialysis three times a
week (7 male, 3 female; mean age 43.4 years, BMI 21.9 kg/m^2, eGFR 4
mL/min/1.73 m^2) were enrolled at Peking University Third Hospital
(Kong 2025 Table 1). All ESRD patients had chronic glomerulonephritis;
diabetes was an exclusion criterion. Serum albumin was 44.9 g/L (HV) and
42.1 g/L (ESRD). The cocktail (midazolam 10 ug, dabigatran etexilate 375 ug,
pitavastatin 10 ug, rosuvastatin 50 ug, atorvastatin 100 ug) was taken
fasted 24 h before dialysis. HV were sampled at 0.5-24 h and ESRD patients
at 1, 4 and 24 h; the 28-h post-dialysis sample was not modelled. One ESRD
patient was excluded from the atorvastatin analysis. The same information is
available from `readModelDb("Kong_2025_pitavastatin")()$population`.

with `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`.

|------|-----------|-------|--------|

# Virtual cohort

Each drug is simulated in 100 HV and 100 ESRD subjects. Serum albumin is
drawn from a normal distribution matching the Table 1 group mean and CV.
The microbiome abundances are not reported per subject, so both are set to
the value at which their effect equals 1 (`log(1.08)` = 0.077%); the
*Veillonella* effect is explored separately below.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20250601)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250601)

n_per_arm <- 100L
obs_times <- c(
  0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24,
  30, 36, 48, 60, 72, 96, 120, 150
)
drugs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~model, ~dose_ug,
  "PTV", "Kong_2025_pitavastatin", 10,
  "DAB", "Kong_2025_dabigatran", 375,
  "RSV", "Kong_2025_rosuvastatin", 50,
  "MDZ", "Kong_2025_midazolam", 10,
  "ATV", "Kong_2025_atorvastatin", 100
)

subjects <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(2 * n_per_arm),
  group = rep(c("HV", "ESRD"), each = n_per_arm),
  RENALIMP_ESRD = rep(c(0L, 1L), each = n_per_arm),
  ALB = c(
    rnorm(n_per_arm, 44.9, 0.08 * 44.9),
    rnorm(n_per_arm, 42.1, 0.04 * 42.1)
  ),
  GUT_VEILLONELLA_PCT = log(1.08),
  GUT_CLOSTRIDIUM_XIVB_PCT = log(1.08)
)

make_events <- function(dose_ug) {
  doses <- subjects |>
    mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose_ug, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(subjects, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(drugs)), function(i) {
  ev <- make_events(drugs$dose_ug[i])
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    readModelDb(drugs$model[i]),
    events = ev,
    keep = c("group")
  ) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(drug = drugs$drug[i])
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(
    drug = factor(drug, levels = drugs$drug),
    group = factor(group, levels = c("HV", "ESRD"))
  )
```

# Replicate Figure 1

Kong 2025 Figure 1 shows the observed concentration-time curves by group
over 0-24 h. The simulated median and 90% prediction interval follow.

```{r figure-1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
sim |>
  filter(time > 0, time <= 24) |>
  group_by(drug, group, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    Q50 = median(Cc),
    Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50, colour = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (pg/mL)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Kong 2025 (median and 90% PI, 100 subjects per group)."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

AUC0-24 and Cmax are computed over 0-24 h (the window of Kong 2025 Table 2,
which reports geometric means of the observed data). AUCinf is computed over
the full 150-h simulation, the window of Kong 2025 Table S7, in which the
authors simulated each participant with the final models.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(drug, group)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(treatment, id, time)

dose_df <- tidyr::crossing(drugs, subjects |> select(id, group)) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(drug, group), time = 0, amt = dose_ug) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0),
  end = c(24, Inf),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  aucinf.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(
  PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals)
)
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Cmax and AUC0-24 references are the observed geometric means of Kong 2025
Table 2; AUCinf references are the geometric means of the authors' own
per-participant simulations (Table S7). Simulated values are medians.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs,
  "PTV HV", 222, 500, 636,
  "PTV ESRD", 246, 922, 1107,
  "DAB HV", 303, 2233, 2533,
  "DAB ESRD", 384, 6872, 19847,
  "RSV HV", 73.0, 591, 1184,
  "RSV ESRD", 58.6, 656, 1656,
  "MDZ HV", 48.8, 121, 145,
  "MDZ ESRD", 16.6, 34.0, 73.0,
  "ATV HV", 23.6, 141, 255,
  "ATV ESRD", 22.0, 181, 282
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "pg/mL", auclast = "h*pg/mL", aucinf.obs = "h*pg/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated (median) vs. published NCA. * differs from the reference by >20%."
)
```

The starred rows are explained by known features of the source rather than
by the model code:

- **Cmax of pitavastatin and atorvastatin.** The fixed ka of 18 1/h for
  pitavastatin and the ka of 7.53 1/h for atorvastatin give an early, sharp
  peak that the HV sampling schedule (first sample at 0.5 h) cannot capture.
  The authors' own simulations show the same overshoot (Table S7 Cmax 313
  and 317 pg/mL for pitavastatin, 45.1 and 52.8 pg/mL for atorvastatin).
- **ESRD Cmax and AUC0-24 of midazolam.** The observed ESRD exposure is
  lower than the model predicts. The ESRD patients were sampled only at 1, 4
  and 24 h, and the Table S7 simulations (AUCinf 73.0 h*pg/mL) agree with the
  model, not with the sparse observed AUC0-24.
- **HV AUC0-24 of atorvastatin.** The model gives a higher exposure than
  the observed NCA (Table 2, 141 h*pg/mL); the authors' own per-participant
  simulations show the same (Table S7 AUClast 253 h*pg/mL in HV).
- **ESRD AUCinf of rosuvastatin.** CL/F depends on the per-subject
  *Clostridium* XIVb abundance, which the paper does not report; this cohort
  holds it at the reference value. The Table S7 ESRD CL/F (30.2 L/h vs
  42.2 L/h in HV) implies higher abundance in the ESRD patients. The ESRD
  AUCinf of pitavastatin is low for the same reason (*Veillonella*), though
  within 20%.

## Typical-value check against the authors' simulations

AUCinf after a single oral dose of a linear model equals dose / (CL/F). The
typical-value AUCinf of each model is compared with the Table S7 geometric
means where the covariates of this cohort fully determine CL/F: all HV groups
(microbiome at the reference value) and the ESRD groups of dabigatran and
midazolam, whose only covariate is ESRD.

```{r typical-check}
typical <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(drugs)), function(i) {
  ev <- make_events(drugs$dose_ug[i]) |>
    filter(id %in% c(1L, n_per_arm + 1L)) |>
    mutate(ALB = 44)
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb(drugs$model[i])),
    events = ev,
    keep = c("group")
  ) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    group_by(group) |>
    summarise(cl = first(cl), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(drug = drugs$drug[i], aucinf = 1000 * drugs$dose_ug[i] / cl)
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(drug, group)) |>
  left_join(published |> select(treatment, ref = aucinf.obs), by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (aucinf - ref) / ref)

knitr::kable(
  typical |>
    select(treatment, cl, aucinf, ref, pct_diff) |>
    rename(
      "Group" = treatment,
      "Typical CL/F (L/h)" = cl,
      "Typical AUCinf (h*pg/mL)" = aucinf,
      "Table S7 AUCinf (h*pg/mL)" = ref,
      "% diff" = pct_diff
    ),
  digits = 1
)

gated <- typical |>
  filter(group == "HV" | drug %in% c("DAB", "MDZ"))
# Deterministic: typical values against the authors' per-participant
# geometric means. Observed spread is -5% to +8%; a mis-transcribed CL/F or
# ESRD shift moves a row by tens of percent.
stopifnot(all(abs(gated$pct_diff) < 15))
```

# Gut *Veillonella* effect on pitavastatin clearance

The Discussion of Kong 2025 states that, together with the direct ESRD
effect, the *Veillonella* term reduces OATP1B-mediated pitavastatin clearance
by 35% at the lowest observed abundance (0.015%), by 54% at 0.52%, and by up
to 75% at the highest (1.42%). Those figures follow from Eq. 1 with the
abundance in percent, which confirms the covariate units.

```{r veillonella, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
mod_ptv <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Kong_2025_pitavastatin"))
theta <- mod_ptv$theta
veil_reduction <- function(veil) {
  100 * (1 - (exp(veil) / 1.08)^theta[["e_gut_veillonella_pct_cl"]] *
    (1 + theta[["e_renalimp_esrd_cl"]]))
}
claims <- tibble(
  veil = c(0.015, 0.52, 1.42),
  paper = c(35, 54, 75),
  model = veil_reduction(veil)
)
knitr::kable(
  claims |>
    rename(
      "Veillonella (%)" = veil,
      "Paper reduction (%)" = paper,
      "Model reduction (%)" = model
    ),
  digits = c(3, 0, 1)
)
stopifnot(all(abs(claims$model - claims$paper) < 1.5))

tibble(veil = seq(0, 1.5, by = 0.01)) |>
  mutate(reduction = veil_reduction(veil)) |>
  ggplot(aes(veil, reduction)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = claims, aes(veil, paper), colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(
    x = "Veillonella relative abundance (%)",
    y = "Reduction in pitavastatin CL/F vs HV (%)",
    caption = "ESRD patients; points are the values quoted in the Kong 2025 Discussion."
  )
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV scale.** Table 3 reports IIV as a percentage, and Eqs. 1-5 print the
  random effect as `e^0.096`, `e^0.225` and so on. The maintainers read the
  percentage as a CV and convert it with `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`; for the
  large values (atorvastatin Vc/F 99.3%, dabigatran Vp/F 86.0%) this gives
  smaller variances than reading the percentage as omega directly.
- **Residual error.** The paper does not report the residual error model or
  its magnitude. `propSd` is fixed at 0 in all five models, so simulations
  are individual predictions; add a residual error before using the models
  for VPCs against observed data.
- **Final estimates vs Eqs. 1-5.** The equations print rounded bootstrap
  medians (e.g. CL/F 17 and exponent -0.68 for pitavastatin); the models use
  the Table 3 final estimates (16.5 and -0.677). The 1.08 normaliser of the
  microbiome terms appears only in the equations and is used as printed for
  both *Veillonella* and *Clostridium* XIVb.
- **Albumin on rosuvastatin Vc/F.** Table 3 gives the coefficient -6.42
  without a functional form. The maintainers encode it as the power form
  (ALB / 44)^-6.42, with 44 g/L the rounded pooled Table 1 mean (43.7 g/L);
  an exponential or linear form with that coefficient would be implausible
  over the observed 40-48 g/L range.
- **Fixed absorption rates.** Pitavastatin ka (18 1/h) and midazolam ka
  (13 1/h) have no RSE and a degenerate bootstrap interval, so they are
  encoded with `fixed()`. Pitavastatin Q/F is printed with RSE 0 but has a
  non-degenerate bootstrap interval (6.6-9.4 L/h), so it is treated as
  estimated. Atorvastatin ka has a bootstrap median of 22 1/h against the
  estimate of 7.53 1/h; the estimate is used.
- **Dabigatran dose.** The model was fitted to dabigatran concentrations
  with the dose expressed as the administered dabigatran etexilate (375 ug);
  the molecular-weight ratio and prodrug conversion are part of CL/F. Enter
  doses as dabigatran etexilate. The typical-value check above (dose/CL =
  2568 vs Table S7 2533 h*pg/mL) confirms this.
- **ESRD and dialysis.** Only pre-dialysis samples were modelled, so the
  models describe the interdialytic period. Table S8 shows that dialysis
  removes dabigatran substantially, which the models do not include.
- **Microbiome covariates.** The per-subject abundances are not reported;
  the virtual cohort holds them at the reference value of 0.077%, which
  understates the ESRD exposure of pitavastatin and, plausibly, of
  rosuvastatin.
- **Errata.** No correction notice was found for Kong 2025 as of
  2026-11-09.
